identity.name: Chlorophylls
identity.chemical_class: Natural magnesium-containing chlorin/porphyrin pigments (chlorophyll a and b)

function.mechanism: Conjugated chlorin/porphyrin ring systems absorb visible light and impart green colour to foods.
common_food_categories: EU-authorised food categories listed under Regulation (EC) No 1333/2008 Annex II/III
In U.S. CFR, chlorophyll-derived sodium copper chlorophyllin is limited to citrus-based dry beverage mixes

adi.basis: EFSA 2015 re-evaluation reported it was not able to derive an ADI for E140(i) from available data.

efsa.key_finding: EFSA re-evaluated chlorophylls (E140(i)), found technical/toxicological data limitations, and did not derive an ADI.

fda.cfr_citation: 21 CFR 73.125 (sodium copper chlorophyllin; chlorophyll-derived color additive)

adi.basis: JECFA database lists ADI as NOT LIMITED for chlorophylls (INS 140).

concerns.summary: EFSA (2015) reported insufficient toxicological/technical data to derive an ADI for E140(i).
A 2021 rat study on tri-sodium copper chlorophyllins reported slight significant genotoxicity at high dose, with lower effects than deltamethrin comparator.
Recent PubMed safety literature is largely on chlorophyllin/copper-complex derivatives and non-food contexts, limiting direct applicability to E140 chlorophylls.

no_concern_confirmed: JECFA database lists ADI as NOT LIMITED for chlorophylls (INS 140).
A 2025 preclinical sodium copper chlorophyllin study reported no acute toxicity up to 5000 mg/kg bw and sub-acute NOAEL indication above 1000 mg/kg bw in tested models.
No chlorophyll/chlorophyllin entry was identified in the current IARC classified-agent dataset.

adi_exceedance.notes: EFSA reported highest estimated exposures in toddlers/children (mean up to 29.0 mg/kg bw/day; high-level up to 51.9 mg/kg bw/day), while ADI was not established.

risk_assessment.rationale: Evidence is mixed: EFSA could not derive an ADI due to data gaps, but E140 remains in regulatory frameworks and JECFA lists ADI as NOT LIMITED. No major IARC or ban signal was identified in the requested sources.
key_factors: EFSA 2015 re-evaluation did not derive an ADI
JECFA ADI listed as NOT LIMITED (INS 140)
U.S. CFR food entry is for chlorophyll-derived sodium copper chlorophyllin (21 CFR 73.125), not a direct E140 listing
Recent PubMed studies are mostly derivative-specific and context-limited
